caption:
बॉलीवुड के दिग्गज एक्टर अनुपम खेर अपनी लाइफस्टाइल को लेकर हमेशा चर्चा में रहते हैं! 😲

हाल ही में एक इंटरव्यू The Unfiltered Hour में अनुपम खेर ने अपनी नेट वर्थ को लेकर इंटरनेट पर चल रही अफवाहों पर खुलकर बात की। एक्टर ने साफ किया कि गूगल पर उनकी नेट वर्थ 400-500 करोड़ रुपये बताई जाती है, जो कि बिल्कुल गलत है। उन्होंने कहा कि उनके पास इस रकम का 10 प्रतिशत भी नहीं है। 💸

इसके साथ ही अनुपम खेर ने किराए के मकान में रहने की वजह भी बताई। उन्होंने 10 साल पहले खुद का घर न खरीदने का फैसला लिया था। एक्टर ने बताया कि उन्होंने मुंबई वाला अपना घर Alia Bhatt को बेच दिया था और तब से वो किराए के घर में रहकर काफी सुकून महसूस करते हैं। 🏠

अनुपम खेर का मानना है कि जायदाद से ज्यादा दिमागी सुकून मायने रखता है। हालांकि, उन्होंने अपनी मां के लिए शिमला में 8 बेडरूम का एक घर खरीदा था क्योंकि उनकी मां हमेशा से अपना घर चाहती थीं। 😇

इतने बड़े एक्टर होने के बावजूद किराए के घर में रहने के अनुपम खेर के इस फैसले पर आपकी क्या राय है? कमेंट्स में जरूर बताइए! 👇

ctx.title: Anupam Kher says internet claims he has Rs 500 cr net worth: ‘I don’t have its 10%; live in rented house’’
ctx.text:
Anupam Kher has often opened up about his conscious lifestyle decision to live in a rented apartment, instead of buying his own house. The veteran actor, who sold his Mumbai home to actress Alia Bhatt years ago, prefers living without the stress of property ownership. In a recent interview, Anupam opened up about feeling ‘liberated’ after taking the decision to live in a rented house. He also called out the internet for spreading false rumours about his net worth being Rs 400-500 crore.
During a conversation with The Unfiltered Hour, Anupam Kher reflected on his life’s choice, calling it ‘liberating’. “From the day I decided to live in a rented apartment, I liberated myself. This was decided ten years ago. I don’t have any property stress, about doing this or that. I only bought one house in Shimla , for my mother. My brother and I both live in a rented apartment, and we are happy about it,” he expressed.
The veteran actor continued, “You feel like the tallest man on Earth; you don’t have any stress on yourself. Before this, when I had a house, I sold it to Alia Bhatt. After that, we shifted to another house. During that same time, Kirron became MP, so she went to Chandigarh . I was looking for a house, and I realised I could keep living in a rented apartment.”
During the interview, Anupam also expressed his disappointment over false reports about his net worth being Rs 400-500 crore, when he doesn’t even have 10% of it. “The perception of me is that I am very rich. If you Google my net worth, you will be shocked. Sometimes, I want to sue them. I don’t even have 10% of Rs 400-500 crore. My friends read on the internet and joke with me to send them something from this amount.”
ALSO READ | Hanuman Ansh director calls out big studios’ silence after Neem Karoli Baba film’s success
However, the actor continues to live a comfortable life, without compromising on the luxuries. “I still like to go to the best restaurants to eat well; I still travel comfortably, and live in the best hotels. It’s not like I live in a hut. I love my comfort. But, there’s no end to this,” he said.
Earlier, during an interaction with The Powerful Humans Official in April this year, Anupam Kher had talked about why he chose not to own a house , while ensuring his mother had one of her own. “I bought a house for my mother because she wanted one in Shimla. One day she told me that she wanted a house in Shimla. She had lived her life in a rented house for 60 years, and now she wanted a home of her own there. We went to Shimla and looked for a house for her. She wanted a one-bedroom place, but I bought her an eight-bedroom house with a hall. These are symbolic things; otherwise how will you set an example?” he asserted.
The actor further explained that he slowly realised that possessions don’t define one’s life. “I am not comparing myself to Gautam Buddha, but he was a prince. When he stepped out into the world, he saw how people lived, and that’s how he became Gautam Buddha. I felt that once you earn money, what do you really need? You need a place to live, whether it’s owned or rented, it’s the same thing. You need a car; you need one or two people to work with you. Beyond that, I can’t eat silver bread or put gold foil on my food. It is called evolvement as a person, I am not saying that I am a saint. When I earned Rs 10,000 for Saransh, today I earn much more—that is a different achievement. We want to see what we can achieve and we go for it.”
Anupam continued, “I felt that when a person passes away, there are often disputes over property, but if you have money to distribute, there is less conflict. I see many elderly people and I am shocked—someone’s son has thrown them out of the house, someone is being pressured to sign a will. There is no such atmosphere in my house, but I believe that the lighter I remain, the higher I can fly.”
